subject: APAC maintenance — temporary p50/p95 measurement window amendment request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenithaitech.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +10:00
Subject: Request: temporary p50/p95 window amendment for APAC maintenance

Hi Neha,

We're planning a controlled data-center migration for our APAC footprint the week of Aug 15. The migration includes DNS cutovers and live state moves for several microservices that talk to Redwood. From our simulation runs, we expect short, concentrated tail latency spikes at p95 for a 2–4 hour window during cutover; p50 should remain stable.

Request: can Redwood temporarily relax the hosted API p95 measurement window for Zenith AI for the maintenance epoch, or allow an exclusion so we aren't counted against SLA for a known 4-hour window? Our intent is to avoid an SLA incident while we complete the migration.

Attached: slo-evidence-peak-graphs.pdf (simulated spike timelines) and migration-runbook-v2.md (high-level steps + rollback).

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
VP Engineering, Zenith AI
Liam@zenithaitech.com

--
Attachment: slo-evidence-peak-graphs.pdf (3 pages, simulated p50/p95 charts)
From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenithaitech.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 17:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p50/p95 window amendment for APAC maintenance

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. A few clarifying items before we can consider a temporary carveout:

- Exact migration timetable (UTC windows) and the proposed exclusion start/end.
- Confirmation of canary / pre-cutover test plan and criteria for rollback.
- Who will be on-call from Zenith during the operation (names/contacts).
- Whether you can adopt our regional fallback (we serve a compatible lower-cost model from another region) as an automatic contingency if latency crosses threshold.

From a contract perspective we can consider a scheduled maintenance exclusion if: the window is well-defined, we have a successful canary, and there are compensating mitigations (fallback + extra logging/traces).

Can you push the exact UTC window and the runbook section that defines rollback criteria? I can loop in Karthik from serving infra for technical feasibility.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0182

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenithaitech.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@zenithaitech.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 02:18:00 +10:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p50/p95 window amendment for APAC maintenance

Hi Neha — thanks for the quick reply. Answers inline and attached updated runbook.

- UTC window: Aug 16, 2026 22:00 UTC -> Aug 17, 2026 02:00 UTC (4 hours) with a canary at 21:30 UTC for 30 minutes.
- Canary criteria: 0.5% error increase AND p95 < 800ms for canary traffic to proceed. Rollback if p95 > 800ms or error rate > 1.5%.
- On-call: Priya N. (priya@zenithaitech.com) and Jae S. (jae@zenithaitech.com), Slack/phone reachable during the window.
- Fallback: we can flip to regional fallback model — engineering has validated compatibility; fallback can be triggered automatically via our orchestration if p95 spikes.

I've attached the updated migration-runbook-v2.md which highlights canary steps and rollback criteria. Also included the simulated peak graphs that show the expected tail behavior under the migration load.

If Redwood can mark the 4-hour window as a scheduled maintenance exclusion (or alternatively widen the p95 measurement window for that epoch to one hour to smooth the spike), that would meet our contract requirements for uptime reporting.

Liam

--
Attachment: migration-runbook-v2.md (runbook excerpt + rollback criteria)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@zenithaitech.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:10:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p50/p95 window amendment for APAC maintenance

Liam — thanks for the detail and for validating the fallback. From an infra standpoint we can support a timeboxed exception provided the following controls are in place:

1) Pre-cutover canary (21:30 UTC) must be observed and green by Redwood's SRE; if not green we do not proceed.
2) Zenith must enable detailed tracing and request-ids for the migration window so we can correlate spikes to your cutover events.
3) Automatic fallback to the regional compatible model must be enabled and tested in the canary.
4) We will treat the 4-hour window as a scheduled maintenance exclusion in reporting only if you provide the final runbook and an on-call roster 48h prior.

Operationally, Karthik proposes: for the epoch Aug 16 22:00 UTC -> Aug 17 02:00 UTC Redwood will apply a temporary SLO measurement change: compute p95 using a 60-minute sliding window for that epoch instead of our default 5-minute bucket, and exclude the 4-hour period from penalty calculations if the canary conditions were met.

We also need a signed addendum on the maintenance window. I'll create a Jira SERV-2143 and attach the runbook — please confirm you can sign the DocuSign by EOD Aug 13.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@zenithaitech.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 23:35:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary p50/p95 window amendment for APAC maintenance — approved (conditional)

Liam — confirmation and next steps. Redwood will approve a conditional maintenance exclusion for Zenith AI for the window Aug 16 22:00 UTC -> Aug 17 02:00 UTC with the following terms: 

- Pre-cutover canary at 21:30 UTC must be executed and observed by Redwood SRE (Karthik) and Zenith on-call.
- If canary is green, Redwood will compute p95 using a 60-minute sliding window for the epoch and exclude the 4-hour maintenance from SLA penalty calculations.
- If the canary fails or if fallback is not enabled/tested, the exclusion will not apply and standard SLO accounting stands.
- Zenith must provide the final runbook and on-call contact list by 2026-08-14 23:59 UTC.
- Redwood will open Jira SERV-2143 (link: https://redwood-prod.atlassian.net/browse/SERV-2143) and provide a DocuSign amendment — please sign before EOD 2026-08-13 to keep timelines.

Action items:
- Liam: upload signed runbook and on-call list (attachment or link).
- Priya/Jae: join the canary Slack channel and be reachable at 21:20 UTC on Aug 16.
- Karthik: run the canary checks and confirm.
- Neha: file the SLA addendum once DocuSign is returned.

I'll attach the runbook to the Jira ticket. Thanks all — we'll reconvene if anything changes.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
